issues.description: The template defines the QFT method with a leading underscore (_qft_circuit_n_qubits) while the problem statement and the solution use qft_circuit_n_qubits (no leading underscore). This name/signature mismatch is structural: students implementing the template method as provided will produce a differently named method than the solution/tests expect, causing confusion and likely failing automated tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method to qft_circuit_n_qubits (remove the leading underscore) so its name/signature matches the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement/tests to reference _qft_circuit_n_qubits consistently.

issues.description: The template defines the QFT-for-n-qubits method with a leading underscore (_qft_circuit_n_qubits) whereas the problem statement, tests, and the solution implementation use qft_circuit_n_qubits (no leading underscore). This mismatch can confuse students: the exercise description and tests expect qft_circuit_n_qubits, but the template's different identifier may cause students to implement the wrong method or be unable to find the correct entry point.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method from _qft_circuit_n_qubits to qft_circuit_n_qubits to match the problem statement, tests, and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem/tests to refer to the underscored name—prefer the first option so the template, tests, and solution use the same public identifier.
